learn.title: Lithium-Ion Battery Storage: Grid Powerhouse
learn.intro: Lithium-ion batteries store energy from renewables, stabilizing grids by balancing supply-demand mismatches and reducing fossil fuel reliance.
learn.c1_text: Batteries store excess solar/wind energy during low demand, releasing it during peaks. A 100MWh battery can power 30,000 homes for 1 hour.
learn.c2_text: They respond in milliseconds to frequency fluctuations, preventing blackouts. Tesla’s Hornsdale project in Australia cut grid instability costs by $150M annually.
learn.c3_text: India plans 150 GW renewable capacity by 2030, requiring 30 GW battery storage to manage intermittency. Current storage capacity is 4.5 GW (2024).
learn.stat2: Global lithium-ion market to hit $1.5T by 2030 (BNEF)

learn.title: Geothermal: Earth’s Hidden Power
learn.intro: Geothermal taps Earth’s heat for 24/7 clean power, reducing fossil fuel use and offering stable baseload energy.
learn.c1_text: Steam or hot water from underground reservoirs drives turbines. The US generates 3.7 GW geothermal power, enough for 2.7 million homes.
learn.c2_text: Beyond electricity, geothermal heats buildings, greenhouses, and districts. Iceland meets 90% of heating needs via geothermal.
learn.c3_text: India has 340 MW potential from 340 sites. Only 0.1% of this is tapped. The Puga Valley project aims to scale this with government support.

learn.title: Floating Solar: Water-Saving Innovation
learn.intro: Floating solar reduces water evaporation, avoids land use conflicts, and boosts efficiency in sunny regions.
learn.c1_text: Cooler water temperatures increase panel efficiency by 5-10%. A 100MW floating farm in France saves 2.5 million m³ of water annually.
learn.c2_text: Utilizes reservoirs, ponds, and wastewater treatment plants. India’s 600MW floating solar target by 2025 avoids 15,000 hectares of land use.
learn.c3_text: India’s 2.5 MW Yamunanagar plant reduced evaporation by 1.2 million m³/year. Target: 10 GW floating solar by 2030.

learn.title: Green Bonds: Climate Finance Engine
learn.intro: Green bonds fund renewable projects, mobilizing $1T+ globally to accelerate clean energy transitions.
learn.c1_text: Proceeds finance wind, solar, and grid upgrades. The World Bank issued $26B in green bonds since 2017.
learn.c2_text: Projects must meet standards like the Green Bond Principles. India’s ₹16,000 crore green bond (2021) funds solar and wind projects.
learn.c3_text: India aims for $50B green bonds by 2030. ₹16,000 crore raised in 2021 funded 1.2 GW renewable projects.

learn.title: Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPOs) in India
learn.intro: RPOs mandate DISCOMs to source 40%+ renewable energy, driving India’s solar and wind growth.
learn.c1_text: RPOs require utilities to buy renewable energy at fixed prices. India’s RPO targets: 20% by 2024-25, 40% by 2030.
learn.c2_text: DISCOMs face penalties for non-compliance. Gujarat’s DISCOM achieved 90% RPO compliance in 2023, reducing coal dependence.
learn.c3_text: RPOs drove 60 GW solar/wind installation (2024). Tamil Nadu’s RPO scheme reduced coal-based generation by 15% (2023).

learn.title: Microgrids: Energy Independence
learn.intro: Microgrids provide reliable power to remote villages and enhance disaster resilience through localized renewable systems.
learn.c1_text: Microgrids combine solar, wind, and storage for off-grid communities. A 100kW microgrid powers 500+ homes in rural India.
learn.c2_text: They operate independently during grid failures. Puerto Rico’s post-Hurricane Maria microgrids restored power in 3 days vs. months.
learn.c3_text: India has 2,500+ microgrids, powering 2 million people. Rajasthan’s 500kW microgrid reduced diesel use by 90%.
